guitar.notes: Eddy Mitchell is a French rock/chanson singer; his backing guitarists changed over decades with no singular documented instrument.

tone.target: warm 50s/60s clean guitar with subtle slapback
tone.profile: warm 50s/60s clean guitar with subtle slapback
tone.summary: A warm, clean signal chain utilizing a US Deluxe or Silver Twin model for classic American pop-rock tone, enhanced with Chorus and Slapback echo to achieve the desired 50s/60s vibe.
corrections: swap subtle reverb for slapback echo
move from jazz/blues to vintage pop/rock

rig.name: Eddy Mitchell - La Dernière Séance - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray hum and noise inherent in vintage-style recordings.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean tones.

blocks.purpose: Slightly lift the mids and overall signal level to cut through the mix without adding grit.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used here for gentle tone shaping, mimicking a clean boost pedal rather than pure volume increase.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal clean and transparent. The 'None' setting ensures no unwanted coloration.
Simulate the classic Fender-style clean American tone (single coils, bright top end).
Provide a bright, focused cabinet sound matching the American clean tone.
blocks.gap: None. Pairs well with US Deluxe.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle movement and width characteristic of 60s pop-rock sounds.
blocks.gap: None. Chorus is perfect for adding vintage sheen.

blocks.purpose: Slightly scoop the low end and enhance the upper mids/treble for clarity and 'air'.
blocks.gap: Using a dedicated EQ to fine-tune the US Deluxe tone, compensating for potential muddiness.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required short slapback echo for a vintage pop feel.
blocks.gap: None. Slapback is ideal for this specific retro effect.

blocks.purpose: Add a very subtle sense of space and warmth without sounding like heavy reverb.
blocks.gap: The Room setting is used sparingly to provide depth, respecting the 'avoid heavy reverb' rule.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default US 2x12 IR for a more period-appropriate, warm vintage speaker simulation.

proposals.recommendedAsset: vintage single-coil cab IR (e.g., Fender Tweed/Blackface)
